findings.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher logic is inverted: returns false when grant shortcut matches and true when it doesn't, so assertions validate the opposite of what they claim
Off-by-one in grant-shortcut extraction in isAccessTokenId matcher: substring(3, 5) should be substring(4, 6) given the 6-char encoded prefix layout, so the matcher can never match a valid token id
getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext NPEs when client session has no user session (e.g. client-credentials grant), breaking token issuance in initToken
Null check duplicated on wrong field in AccessTokenContext constructor: rawTokenId is never null-checked due to copy-paste bug, allowing null raw id to propagate into the jti
Removing the public OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor breaks the SPI for existing custom grant extensions with no deprecation cycle

New OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor derives grantType from form params, silently changing behavior of existing subclasses and causing encodeTokenId to throw IllegalStateException for grants whose form param doesn't match a registered factory id

Lazy registry refresh in getShortcutByGrantType / getGrantTypeByShortcut can race inconsistently and duplicate-shortcut collisions silently overwrite mappings, causing tokens encoded with one grant to decode as another grant type

Uncontrolled user input flows into token ID encoding paths: getShortcutByGrantType()/getGrantTypeByShortcut() return null for grant types failing lazy refresh, causing encodeTokenId() to throw IllegalStateException and getTokenContextFromTokenId() to throw IllegalArgumentException, turning token minting into a 500 for legitimate flows

Breaking SPI change: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() added as a new abstract method on an interface implemented by external grant-type extensions, causing AbstractMethodError or provider-registration failure for existing custom grants; it should have been a default method

Test matcher logic in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId is inverted (returns false on match) and reads wrong character positions: substring(3, 5) compares the wrong slice since the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 of the 6-char prefix

Duplicated-shortcut detection in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() only happens at startup and only detects collisions; a factory returning null shortcut silently maps null keys and the size check does not fire

Constructor validation bug in AccessTokenContext: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType) called twice while rawTokenId is never null-checked (second requireNonNull checks the wrong field), allowing malformed token ID 'xxxxxx:null'
Information disclosure in token IDs: encoded prefix revealing session state and grant type is visible in plaintext in every access token jti, breaking the assumption that jti is an opaque UUID

Parsing attacker-influenced identifiers throws uncaught runtime exceptions: getTokenContextFromTokenId() throws IllegalArgumentException for unknown shortcuts in 6-char-prefixed IDs instead of degrading to UNKNOWN as it does for legacy IDs

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut: uncached miss causes full provider-factory registry scan on every call for unknown shortcuts, enabling cheap CPU-amplification/DoS on hot token-validation paths; needs a negative-result cache

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException on unresolvable shortcuts, making tokens issued before a grant provider was removed/undeployed unparseable; should degrade to UNKNOWN instead of throwing
AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId: inverted match logic returns false when the grant shortcut matches, so the matcher can never succeed
AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId: wrong substring index — grant shortcut is chars 4-5 (substring(4, 6)) but code uses substring(3, 5)

AccessTokenContext constructor: Objects.requireNonNull checks grantType again with message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' instead of checking rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId to pass construction and fail later

Token ID inflation: 7-char prefix added to every access-token jti and all stores holding token IDs (admin events, Details.TOKEN_ID, revocation lookups, user-session notes, audit logs), a constant-size storage/memory increase on 100% of issued tokens

jti claim format changes from plain UUID to '<6-char-context>:<uuid>' in TokenManager.initToken (~line 1051), a breaking change to the external token contract with no migration flag or transition period for mixed-format tokens during rolling upgrades

Adding abstract getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation breaks third-party implementers at compile time and causes AbstractMethodError at runtime during postInit in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory for all realms
OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor removed from public SPI class OAuth2GrantType (~line 99), breaking binary compatibility (NoSuchMethodError) for external code calling it

grantType in Context is read from formParams in the constructor before setFormParams() may be called, so callers populating params after construction get null grantType that silently becomes 'na' in the token id
getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException on hard length check (!= 6) or unknown shortcut when parsing untrusted external token IDs instead of degrading to UNKNOWN
Off-by-one in isAccessTokenId test matcher in AssertEvents.java (~line 473): uses substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6), comparing the wrong substring for grant type

rawTokenId null check in AccessTokenContext constructor duplicates the grantType check (Objects.requireNonNull called on grantType twice), so a null rawTokenId slips past validation and produces encodeTokenId output like 'onrtac:null'

Inverted matcher logic in `isAccessTokenId` (AssertEvents.java:~478): returns false when the grant shortcut matches and true when it does not, the exact inverse of the intended assertion, causing tests to fail on valid token IDs and pass on wrong ones

Wrong substring indices for grant shortcut (AssertEvents.java:~477): code uses `substring(3, 5)` but the grant type occupies characters 4–6, so it should be `substring(4, 6)`; the comment also contradicts the code

Duplicate null-check for `grantType` in AccessTokenContext constructor (copy-paste) means `rawTokenId` is never validated and can be null, flowing into `encodeTokenId` producing token IDs ending in ":null"

Unbounded lazy cache population from untrusted input in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType / getGrantTypeByShortcut: unknown grant-type names reaching encodeTokenId are cached after a factory scan and repeated distinct values could grow the maps without bound and add per-request scan latency

`encodeTokenId` throws IllegalStateException on unresolvable grant type, causing token issuance (TokenManager.initToken) to fail with a 500 instead of degrading to the UNKNOWN/"na" encoding used elsewhere

Duplicate-shortcut validation via map-size comparison in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit is fragile: conflates same-ID and same-shortcut collisions and gives no message identifying the offending factories

Context.grantType captured before dispatch in OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor may diverge from the actual grant executed (e.g., token exchange), recording the client-requested grant rather than the grant actually executed in token metadata

isAccessTokenId matcher in AssertEvents.java has inverted matching logic: it returns false when the grant shortcut matches the expected value, so all expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthreqIdToToken assertions assert the opposite of intent (P1)

Unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest hand-populates factory maps with only ro/cc and never calls postInit, so real shortcut registration, duplicate-shortcut collision detection, lazy re-lookups, and UNKNOWN handling are untested (P2)

Behavioral change to jti/token ID format (plain UUID to xx:uuid prefixed format in TokenManager.initToken) has no end-to-end integration test covering authorization-code flow, refresh-token path, lightweight/offline tokens, or token exchange (P1)

testIncorrectGrantType catches generic RuntimeException and ignores it, so any unexpected failure passes; should assert IllegalArgumentException with specific message 'Unknown value 'ac' for grant type' (P3)

Inverted condition in test matcher isAccessTokenId (AssertEvents.java ~line 476-484): substring(3,5).equals check returns false when grant shortcut matches, inverting the intent of expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions
Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext constructor (~line 65): Objects.requireNonNull called twice on grantType, so rawTokenId is never null-checked

TokenContextEncoderProvider/Factory/SPI placed in services module but exported as SPI via META-INF/services, forcing third-party implementations to compile against keycloak-services; SPI interfaces typically belong in server-spi/server-spi-private

Removal of OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context) copy constructor is a breaking API change for third-party subclasses/callers in server-spi-private, and it is the second removal within the same release line
Constants.GRANT_TYPE aliases OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE creating two names for one attribute key, risking split usage and undocumented duplication

Client-session-context Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute silently ignored/stale for unknown grants during refresh flow; combined with encoder throwing IllegalStateException for unmapped grants, tokens under unregistered grant types fail at issue time instead of degrading gracefully

Duplicated 'unknown' sentinel constants across classes ("na" grant, "un" session/token shortcuts, UNKNOWN enums) conflate parse-failure with valid state in the domain object, forcing encode-side IllegalStateException guards
getShouldUseLightweightToken made public static solely for cross-package reuse, indicating a layering leak between mappers and encoder packages; should move to a shared location

Non-final mutable package-private maps grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts exposed for test injection; test bypasses postInit including duplicate-shortcut validation, allowing tested setup to diverge from production

Inconsistent grant shortcut definitions: ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantTypeFactory, PermissionGrantTypeFactory, TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory use inline string literals while others define GRANT_SHORTCUT constants, inviting magic-string drift

Duplicate-shortcut validation in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit only detects size mismatch; a grant with "na" shortcut silently collides with the UNKNOWN sentinel mapping without detection

Inverted assertion in isAccessTokenId matcher in AssertEvents.java: returns false when the grant shortcut matches the expected grant and true when it does not, causing tests to fail on correct behavior and pass on wrong grant types
substring(3, 5) in isAccessTokenId should be substring(4, 6) for a grant shortcut at offset 4
items[0] shorter than 5 chars in isAccessTokenId throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of mismatching
AccessTokenContext constructor null check duplicated on grantType instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId to produce a token id like "onrtna:null"

Lazy map refresh paths in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut blindly put into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without re-checking for collisions, silently overwriting shortcuts on hot-deployed grants
Public Context(Context) copy constructor removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context, breaking existing third-party grant SPI implementations at runtime with NoSuchMethodError
Remaining OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor NPEs if formParams is null, which the old copy constructor tolerated

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId throws unhandled IllegalArgumentException on malformed token ids containing a ':' with a prefix not exactly 6 chars, instead of graceful UNKNOWN handling

getGrantTypeByShortcut/getShortcutByGrantType are non-atomic check-then-act: concurrent requests can race on lazy map population, leaving grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts temporarily inconsistent

PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process() sets GRANT_TYPE on a locally created DefaultClientSessionContext that doesn't flow through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, so the attribute may not reach initToken and the encoded id may silently carry "na" instead of "pc"

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher logic is inverted: returns false when grant shortcut matches and true when it doesn't, so assertions validate the opposite of what they claim
Off-by-one in grant-shortcut extraction in isAccessTokenId matcher: substring(3, 5) should be substring(4, 6) given the 6-char encoded prefix layout, so the matcher can never match a valid token id

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the encoded prefix is 6 chars (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantType), as enforced by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId (substring(4,6) for grant shortcut). The matcher instead uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which grabs the last char of tokenType + first char of grantType, so it cannot correctly extract the 2-char grant shortcut from a valid token id (e.g., "trltcc"). This is a verifiable off-by-one defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext NPEs when client session has no user session (e.g. client-credentials grant), breaking token issuance in initToken

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, the code unconditionally does `UserSessionModel userSession = clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession();` and then immediately dereferences it (`userSession.getPersistenceState()`, `userSession.isOffline()`). If any flow can produce a ClientSessionContext whose clientSession has no UserSessionModel, this will NPE during TokenManager.initToken (which now always calls `encoder.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)`). The diff itself doesn’t prove that client-credentials (or any other grant) actually has a null userSession in practice, but the new logic clearly lacks a null-safe fallback (e.g., mapping to SessionType.UNKNOWN), making this a concrete edge-case risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Null check duplicated on wrong field in AccessTokenContext constructor: rawTokenId is never null-checked due to copy-paste bug, allowing null raw id to propagate into the jti
Removing the public OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor breaks the SPI for existing custom grant extensions with no deprecation cycle

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previously public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (in `server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantType.java`). Any existing grant implementations (including external extensions compiled against this API) that call `new OAuth2GrantType.Context(existingContext)` will no longer compile / link. The diff shows no replacement copy/clone mechanism, so this is a concrete API compatibility break (even if core code was updated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: New OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor derives grantType from form params, silently changing behavior of existing subclasses and causing encodeTokenId to throw IllegalStateException for grants whose form param doesn't match a registered factory id

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `grantType` to `OAuth2GrantType.Context` and initializes it from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, and `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse(...)` stores it into `clientSessionCtx` (Constants.GRANT_TYPE). However, the new encoding path does not inherently “silently” break existing grants: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)` explicitly converts a missing/null attribute to `UNKNOWN` (`"na"`), and the factory maps `UNKNOWN` to itself, so `encodeTokenId(...)` will not throw just because the form param is absent. Also, for normal flows the `grant_type` form param is the same value used to select the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (its `getId()`), which is exactly what `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` indexes when building `grantsToShortcuts`, so the claimed mismatch/IllegalStateException is not demonstrated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lazy registry refresh in getShortcutByGrantType / getGrantTypeByShortcut can race inconsistently and duplicate-shortcut collisions silently overwrite mappings, causing tokens encoded with one grant to decode as another grant type

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds lazy refresh paths in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() that update ConcurrentHashMap mappings via plain put() without re-validating shortcut uniqueness. While initial collisions are detected in postInit() by comparing grantsByShortcuts vs grantsToShortcuts sizes (and would throw), a later “new grant type was deployed” refresh can silently overwrite an existing shortcut->grant mapping, which could make decoding of an already-issued token’s shortcut resolve to a different grant type. The finding’s broad claim about racing is plausible (non-atomic check-then-put), but the diff does not show an actual race bug under normal (non-colliding) shortcuts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Uncontrolled user input flows into token ID encoding paths: getShortcutByGrantType()/getGrantTypeByShortcut() return null for grant types failing lazy refresh, causing encodeTokenId() to throw IllegalStateException and getTokenContextFromTokenId() to throw IllegalArgumentException, turning token minting into a 500 for legitimate flows

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add encoding/decoding that can throw when a grant type/shortcut is unknown (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() throws if getShortcutByGrantType() returns null; getTokenContextFromTokenId() throws if shortcut unmapped). However, from the diff alone there’s no verifiable path where *legitimate token minting* would hit this due to uncontrolled user input: grantType is read from formParams into Context, but when it’s missing/null it is normalized to UNKNOWN (“na”) before encoding, and supported grants are preloaded in postInit() and additionally lazy-refreshed via sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(...). Whether an attacker can supply an unsupported grant_type and still reach createTokenResponse/initToken is not shown in this PR diff, so the claim that this “turns token minting into a 500 for legitimate flows” isn’t grounded by the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking SPI change: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() added as a new abstract method on an interface implemented by external grant-type extensions, causing AbstractMethodError or provider-registration failure for existing custom grants; it should have been a default method

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (server-spi-private) without providing a default implementation. This is a binary-incompatible SPI change: any existing `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation compiled against the old interface would fail to load/link (e.g., `AbstractMethodError`) until updated. While this is in `server-spi-private` (so arguably not a supported public extension point), the compatibility concern itself is real and directly grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test matcher logic in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId is inverted (returns false on match) and reads wrong character positions: substring(3, 5) compares the wrong slice since the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 of the 6-char prefix
matched_golden_ids: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same two defects as the golden comment: (1) the match logic is inverted (returns false when it should return true on a grant shortcut/UUID match), and (2) the substring indices are wrong, noting the grant shortcut should be taken from indices 4–5 (i.e., substring(4,6)) rather than an earlier slice (substring(3,5)).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated-shortcut detection in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() only happens at startup and only detects collisions; a factory returning null shortcut silently maps null keys and the size check does not fire

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), both grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts are ConcurrentHashMap. ConcurrentHashMap does not allow null keys/values, so a factory returning a null shortcut would not be “silently mapped”; it would throw a NullPointerException at put(grantShortcut, grantName). Also, shortcut-collision detection via the size mismatch check would still fire for duplicate non-null shortcuts because grantsByShortcuts would overwrite an entry while grantsToShortcuts would keep both grant IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Constructor validation bug in AccessTokenContext: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType) called twice while rawTokenId is never null-checked (second requireNonNull checks the wrong field), allowing malformed token ID 'xxxxxx:null'
Information disclosure in token IDs: encoded prefix revealing session state and grant type is visible in plaintext in every access token jti, breaking the assumption that jti is an opaque UUID

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally changes access token IDs from a raw generated ID to a prefixed, human-decodable format. In `TokenManager.initToken`, `token.id(...)` is now set via `encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` encodes `sessionType` + `tokenType` + `grantShort` + ':' + `rawTokenId` (e.g., `trltcc:UUID`). This does expose session state/grant type in plaintext and no longer guarantees `jti` is an opaque UUID (tests were updated from `isUUID()` to `isAccessTokenId(...)` accordingly). However, the change is clearly purposeful per the new SPI/provider Javadoc, and the diff alone doesn’t establish that this violates a required security property; it’s more a compatibility/architecture concern for consumers assuming UUID-only `jti`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Parsing attacker-influenced identifiers throws uncaught runtime exceptions: getTokenContextFromTokenId() throws IllegalArgumentException for unknown shortcuts in 6-char-prefixed IDs instead of degrading to UNKNOWN as it does for legacy IDs

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` returns UNKNOWN only for legacy IDs without `:` but throws `IllegalArgumentException` for malformed/unknown 6-char prefixes (bad length, unknown sessionType/tokenType/grantType shortcuts). This is intentional per the added test `testIncorrectGrantType()` which expects a runtime exception. However, it is a robustness/DoS concern if this parser is ever invoked on untrusted token IDs without catching exceptions; that impact is not demonstrated in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut: uncached miss causes full provider-factory registry scan on every call for unknown shortcuts, enabling cheap CPU-amplification/DoS on hot token-validation paths; needs a negative-result cache

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut, if grantsByShortcuts.get(shortcut) returns null, it does a sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class) scan and only updates the maps when a matching factory is found. When the shortcut is truly unknown (or attacker-supplied garbage in an encoded token id), nothing is cached, so repeated calls for the same unknown shortcut will re-scan the provider-factory stream every time. The diff doesn’t prove this method is invoked on a hot token-validation path, but the repeated full scan-on-miss behavior for unknown shortcuts is real and could warrant a negative-result cache.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException on unresolvable shortcuts, making tokens issued before a grant provider was removed/undeployed unparseable; should degrade to UNKNOWN instead of throwing

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId, when the encoded token id contains a context prefix (has ':') and the grant-type shortcut cannot be resolved (factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut returns null), the code throws IllegalArgumentException rather than falling back to UNKNOWN ("na"). This is grounded in the explicit null checks and throws for st/tt/gt shortcuts. The finding’s scenario (a shortcut becoming unresolvable after a grant provider is removed/undeployed) is plausible from the diff because grant shortcuts are populated from deployed OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit/getGrantTypeByShortcut, but whether throwing is a true defect vs an intentional strictness/compatibility choice cannot be fully confirmed from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId: inverted match logic returns false when the grant shortcut matches, so the matcher can never succeed

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId.matchesSafely, the logic is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` causes the matcher to fail when the grant shortcut *does* match, so it cannot ever succeed for the expected shortcut. This is directly verifiable in the added method in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId: wrong substring index — grant shortcut is chars 4-5 (substring(4, 6)) but code uses substring(3, 5)

adjudication.rationale: In TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(), the encoded context is 6 chars: sessionType(0-1) + tokenType(2-3) + grantShortcut(4-5). Therefore the grant shortcut should be extracted with substring(4, 6). However AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId() uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which is off by one and will not read the correct 2-char grant shortcut from the 6-char prefix.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext constructor: Objects.requireNonNull checks grantType again with message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' instead of checking rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId to pass construction and fail later
matched_golden_ids: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same constructor bug: the fourth Objects.requireNonNull mistakenly validates grantType again (despite the rawTokenId message) instead of validating rawTokenId, letting null rawTokenId pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Token ID inflation: 7-char prefix added to every access-token jti and all stores holding token IDs (admin events, Details.TOKEN_ID, revocation lookups, user-session notes, audit logs), a constant-size storage/memory increase on 100% of issued tokens

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes access-token `jti` generation to prepend encoded context: `TokenManager.initToken()` now builds an `AccessTokenContext` and sets `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` returns a 6-char context + `':'` + raw UUID (7 extra chars total). This is a constant-size increase applied to (at least) every issued access token ID, which will propagate to any logs/events/stores that persist `jti` (e.g., tests were updated to expect a prefixed `Details.TOKEN_ID`). This is a real, diff-grounded performance/storage/compatibility concern but not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: jti claim format changes from plain UUID to '<6-char-context>:<uuid>' in TokenManager.initToken (~line 1051), a breaking change to the external token contract with no migration flag or transition period for mixed-format tokens during rolling upgrades

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the access token ID/JTI generation in `TokenManager.initToken`: it no longer sets `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` but instead encodes a context prefix via `TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)`, producing a format like `<6-char-context>:<raw-uuid>` (see `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`). There is no flag/config shown to retain the previous plain-UUID format, so this is a concrete external-contract/compatibility concern. However, the diff alone does not prove this breaks token validation/behavior (JTI is often treated as opaque), so it’s better classified as a significant compatibility/upgrade concern rather than a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding abstract getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation breaks third-party implementers at compile time and causes AbstractMethodError at runtime during postInit in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory for all realms

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface with no default implementation. This is a binary- and source-incompatible change for any existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations (they will fail to compile until updated; already-compiled implementations will lack the method). The new `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)` unconditionally casts each factory to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` and calls `gtf.getShortcut()`, which would trigger an `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when encountering an older implementation missing the method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor removed from public SPI class OAuth2GrantType (~line 99), breaking binary compatibility (NoSuchMethodError) for external code calling it

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `OAuth2GrantType.Context` (see removal block in `OAuth2GrantType.java` around the constructor list). That is an API/binary-compatibility break for any already-compiled code that invoked this constructor (would manifest as `NoSuchMethodError` at runtime). However, the diff alone can’t prove whether this class is intended as a stable *public* SPI for external consumers (it lives in `server-spi-private`), so the impact is a compatibility/extension concern rather than a directly verifiable functional defect in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: grantType in Context is read from formParams in the constructor before setFormParams() may be called, so callers populating params after construction get null grantType that silently becomes 'na' in the token id

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, `grantType` is initialized once in the constructor from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, but the class still exposes `setFormParams(...)` and that setter does not recompute/update `grantType`. Therefore, any code path that constructs `Context` with incomplete/empty `formParams` and later calls `setFormParams()` will have `getGrantType()` remain null/stale. This null then propagates to `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` (e.g., `OAuth2GrantTypeBase#createTokenResponse`) and ultimately becomes `UNKNOWN`/`"na"` in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`, matching the finding’s described silent fallback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException on hard length check (!= 6) or unknown shortcut when parsing untrusted external token IDs instead of degrading to UNKNOWN

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` explicitly throws `IllegalArgumentException` when `encodedContext.length() != 6` and when any shortcut (session/token/grant) is unknown, rather than degrading to `UNKNOWN` (it only degrades when there is no `:` at all). This matches the finding. However, the diff does not show this method being invoked on untrusted external token IDs in a way that would cause broken behavior; it may be an intentional strict-parse choice since token IDs are generated internally via `encodeTokenId(...)` and old tokens without `:` are handled. So it’s a valid robustness/edge-case concern created by the change, but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one in isAccessTokenId test matcher in AssertEvents.java (~line 473): uses substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6), comparing the wrong substring for grant type

adjudication.rationale: The token id encoding introduced in this diff is `sessionType(2 chars) + tokenType(2 chars) + grantShortcut(2 chars) + ':' + rawId` (see `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`, which concatenates two 2-char shortcuts plus a 2-char grant shortcut, total 6 chars before `:`). Therefore the grant shortcut occupies indices `[4,6)` in the prefix. However, `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` extracts `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, which grabs the 4th and 5th characters (0-based indices 3 and 4), i.e., part of the tokenType + part of the grant shortcut, so it compares the wrong substring for grant type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: rawTokenId null check in AccessTokenContext constructor duplicates the grantType check (Objects.requireNonNull called on grantType twice), so a null rawTokenId slips past validation and produces encodeTokenId output like 'onrtac:null'

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the last null check mistakenly calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null and still construct an instance, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` will then concatenate it into the token id (Java string concatenation yields `"null"`), producing values like `"...:null"`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted matcher logic in `isAccessTokenId` (AssertEvents.java:~478): returns false when the grant shortcut matches and true when it does not, the exact inverse of the intended assertion, causing tests to fail on valid token IDs and pass on wrong ones

adjudication.rationale:
In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the matcher explicitly returns `false` when the extracted shortcut equals `expectedGrantShortcut`:
```java
if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
```
This inverts the intended assertion (it should fail when it does *not* match). As written, valid token IDs with the expected grant shortcut are rejected, while mismatching shortcuts can still pass as long as the part after `:` is a UUID (`return isUUID().matches(items[1])`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong substring indices for grant shortcut (AssertEvents.java:~477): code uses `substring(3, 5)` but the grant type occupies characters 4–6, so it should be `substring(4, 6)`; the comment also contradicts the code

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the encoded context is 6 chars (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantType) per DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider; the grant shortcut therefore starts at index 4, so using items[0].substring(3, 5) is incorrect and contradicts the comment about the grant being the 4th+ chars. This would mis-parse the grant shortcut and break the matcher logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate null-check for `grantType` in AccessTokenContext constructor (copy-paste) means `rawTokenId` is never validated and can be null, flowing into `encodeTokenId` producing token IDs ending in ":null"

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the null-check intended for `rawTokenId` is a copy/paste error: it calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null without being validated, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` later concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would produce an encoded token id ending with `:null` if an `AccessTokenContext` is ever constructed with a null rawTokenId.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded lazy cache population from untrusted input in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType / getGrantTypeByShortcut: unknown grant-type names reaching encodeTokenId are cached after a factory scan and repeated distinct values could grow the maps without bound and add per-request scan latency

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType, the maps are only populated lazily when sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(OAuth2GrantType.class, grantType) returns a non-null factory (i.e., the grant type is actually deployed/known). If an untrusted/unknown grant_type arrives (e.g., from formParams), it is not cached; instead encodeTokenId will later throw due to grantShort == null. Similarly, getGrantTypeByShortcut only inserts when the shortcut matches an existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. Therefore repeated distinct untrusted values cannot cause unbounded growth of the maps as claimed. At most, unknown shortcuts/grant types can trigger repeated lookups/scans without negative-result caching, which is a performance concern, not unbounded cache growth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `encodeTokenId` throws IllegalStateException on unresolvable grant type, causing token issuance (TokenManager.initToken) to fail with a 500 instead of degrading to the UNKNOWN/"na" encoding used elsewhere

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that token issuance now depends on `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)`, which throws `IllegalStateException` when `factory.getShortcutByGrantType(tokenContext.getGrantType())` returns null (i.e., when the grant type cannot be mapped to a 2-char shortcut). `TokenManager.initToken` calls `encodeTokenId(...)` directly, so such an exception would propagate and fail issuance. However, the diff also adds `UNKNOWN` ("na") handling and wires `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` from known flows, and the factory populates mappings from all `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations (now required to provide `getShortcut()`), so under normal/expected configurations this should not occur; it’s more of a robustness/extensibility edge-case than a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-shortcut validation via map-size comparison in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit is fragile: conflates same-ID and same-shortcut collisions and gives no message identifying the offending factories

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, duplicate detection relies on comparing grantsByShortcuts.size() vs grantsToShortcuts.size(). Because both maps are populated via put(), collisions overwrite entries. If there are collisions in both dimensions (duplicate shortcut and duplicate grant ID), the overwrites can reduce both map sizes equally, causing the size comparison to pass even though duplicates exist (e.g., factories with (id1,sh1), (id2,sh1), (id2,sh2) yield equal sizes). This can silently allow ambiguous mappings and later incorrect encode/decode behavior. The finding’s point about conflating collision types and not identifying offenders is also grounded in the generic exception message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Context.grantType captured before dispatch in OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor may diverge from the actual grant executed (e.g., token exchange), recording the client-requested grant rather than the grant actually executed in token metadata

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType` is set from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)` and then used by grant implementations (via `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`) to store `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` in `ClientSessionContext`. This value is the same parameter used to dispatch/select the grant type in the token endpoint, so there is no diff-grounded evidence it would diverge from the actually executed grant. Additionally, for flows that might not use `OAuth2GrantType.Context` (e.g., token exchange handled in `StandardTokenExchangeProvider`), the code explicitly sets `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE)`, which aligns metadata with the executed operation rather than the captured context value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId matcher in AssertEvents.java has inverted matching logic: it returns false when the grant shortcut matches the expected value, so all expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthreqIdToToken assertions assert the opposite of intent (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the matcher returns false when the parsed grant shortcut equals the expected value: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. This inverts the intended assertion logic, causing expectations like `expectCodeToToken(...).detail(Details.TOKEN_ID, isAccessTokenId(...))` to fail for correct token IDs and potentially pass for incorrect ones. (Additionally, the substring indices `(3,5)` don’t align with the comment/encoding elsewhere, but the inverted equality check alone is a verifiable defect.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest hand-populates factory maps with only ro/cc and never calls postInit, so real shortcut registration, duplicate-shortcut collision detection, lazy re-lookups, and UNKNOWN handling are untested (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before()` initializes `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` with `init(null)` but then manually assigns `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` to contain only `ro`, `cc`, and `na`, and never calls `postInit(...)`. As a result, code added in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)` (real grant shortcut discovery via `getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)` and the duplicate-shortcut validation comparing map sizes) is not exercised, nor is the factory’s lazy refresh logic in `getShortcutByGrantType` / `getGrantTypeByShortcut` that depends on `sessionFactory`. However, the finding’s claim that UNKNOWN handling is untested is incorrect, since `testUnknownGrantType()` explicitly covers the `na` case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change to jti/token ID format (plain UUID to xx:uuid prefixed format in TokenManager.initToken) has no end-to-end integration test covering authorization-code flow, refresh-token path, lightweight/offline tokens, or token exchange (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* add/adjust end-to-end integration assertions for the new access-token ID/jti format in several flows: AssertEvents now expects `Details.TOKEN_ID` via `isAccessTokenId(...)` for authorization-code (`expectCodeToToken`), refresh-token (`expectRefresh`), device-code, and CIBA flows. There is also a new unit test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` covering encoding/decoding including offline/transient + lightweight/regular combinations. While token exchange isn’t explicitly asserted in this diff, the finding’s broad claim that there is no E2E coverage for auth-code/refresh/etc. is contradicted by the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testIncorrectGrantType catches generic RuntimeException and ignores it, so any unexpected failure passes; should assert IllegalArgumentException with specific message 'Unknown value 'ac' for grant type' (P3)
matched_golden_ids: Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the test is catching a generic RuntimeException, making the test too permissive, and recommend asserting/catching the specific IllegalArgumentException (optionally with a message) for precise testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted condition in test matcher isAccessTokenId (AssertEvents.java ~line 476-484): substring(3,5).equals check returns false when grant shortcut matches, inverting the intent of expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the matcher returns false when the extracted grant shortcut equals the expected shortcut: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, which inverts the intended assertion. Additionally, given the encoded context is 6 chars (2 session + 2 token + 2 grant), the grant shortcut should be at indices [4,6), not substring(3,5), further breaking correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext constructor (~line 65): Objects.requireNonNull called twice on grantType, so rawTokenId is never null-checked

adjudication.rationale: In the new file AccessTokenContext.java, the constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice: the 4th check intends to validate rawTokenId (message says "Null rawTokenId not allowed") but mistakenly checks grantType again, leaving rawTokenId unchecked and allowing null rawTokenId to pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TokenContextEncoderProvider/Factory/SPI placed in services module but exported as SPI via META-INF/services, forcing third-party implementations to compile against keycloak-services; SPI interfaces typically belong in server-spi/server-spi-private

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new SPI (`TokenContextEncoderSpi`) and its provider/factory interfaces under `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/*` and registers them via `META-INF/services/...` and `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.provider.Spi`. This means any custom implementation of `TokenContextEncoderProvider(Factory)` must compile against the `services` module where those interfaces live, rather than a lighter-weight SPI module. However, the finding’s “third-party” angle is somewhat weakened by `TokenContextEncoderSpi.isInternal()` returning `true`, suggesting it may not be intended for external implementations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context) copy constructor is a breaking API change for third-party subclasses/callers in server-spi-private, and it is the second removal within the same release line

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (server-spi-private). Any external code (including third-party grant implementations) that previously instantiated a new `Context` by copying an existing one will no longer compile and would be a source/binary compatibility break. The claim that it is the "second removal within the same release line" is not verifiable from this diff, but the constructor removal itself is directly shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Constants.GRANT_TYPE aliases OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE creating two names for one attribute key, risking split usage and undocumented duplication

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Constants.GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE`, which is an alias to the same underlying string value, not a second distinct attribute key. Using either constant would set/get the same `ClientSessionContext` attribute, so the stated risk of “split usage” causing duplication/broken behavior is not evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-session-context Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute silently ignored/stale for unknown grants during refresh flow; combined with encoder throwing IllegalStateException for unmapped grants, tokens under unregistered grant types fail at issue time instead of degrading gracefully

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows refresh flow explicitly sets the clientSessionCtx attribute `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` to `OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN` (TokenManager.validateToken), so it is not “silently ignored/stale” during refresh; it is deliberately set. Also, the encoder’s grant-type shortcut map is populated from all registered `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()`, so for any grant that can actually be processed (i.e., has a registered factory), `encodeTokenId()` should have a mapping and will not throw. The finding’s failure scenario depends on a grant type being used without a registered factory/shortcut mapping, but such a grant would not be reachable via the normal grant processing path shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated 'unknown' sentinel constants across classes ("na" grant, "un" session/token shortcuts, UNKNOWN enums) conflate parse-failure with valid state in the domain object, forcing encode-side IllegalStateException guards

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally models “unknown/old token” cases as valid `AccessTokenContext` values (e.g., `SessionType.UNKNOWN("un")`, `TokenType.UNKNOWN("un")`, and grant-type sentinel `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN = "na"`). `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` returns these UNKNOWN states for legacy token IDs without a `:` (backward compatibility), and `encodeTokenId()` then has explicit guards that throw `IllegalStateException` for UNKNOWN session/token types while allowing the "na" grant (validated by `testOldToken()` and `testUnknownGrantType()`). This matches the finding as an architectural/domain-model concern (unknown states used to represent parse/legacy conditions and requiring encode-side guards), but it is not a verifiable functional defect in the diff since the behavior is deliberate and covered by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getShouldUseLightweightToken made public static solely for cross-package reuse, indicating a layering leak between mappers and encoder packages; should move to a shared location

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken` from package-private to `public static` (services/.../mappers/AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java) and the new encoder (`services/.../encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java`) calls `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`. This is concrete cross-package reuse enabled by widening visibility, creating tighter coupling between the mappers package and the new encoder SPI. That’s an architectural/layering concern, but not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-final mutable package-private maps grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts exposed for test injection; test bypasses postInit including duplicate-shortcut validation, allowing tested setup to diverge from production

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, the maps `grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts` are declared with no access modifier (package-private) and are mutable/non-final. The unit test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` directly assigns to these fields (`factory.grantsByShortcuts = new HashMap<>(); ... factory.grantsToShortcuts = ...`) instead of exercising the production `postInit(...)` path, which is where duplicate-shortcut validation happens (`if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()) throw ...`). This is a test/encapsulation concern (tests can diverge from production initialization) but not a directly verifiable runtime defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent grant shortcut definitions: ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantTypeFactory, PermissionGrantTypeFactory, TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory use inline string literals while others define GRANT_SHORTCUT constants, inviting magic-string drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show mixed approaches: e.g., AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory/RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory/CibaGrantTypeFactory/DeviceGrantTypeFactory define GRANT_SHORTCUT constants, while ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory/ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantTypeFactory/PermissionGrantTypeFactory/TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory return inline literals ("cc","ro","pg","te"). However, this is a consistency/style concern (“magic strings”) and the diff does not show any resulting incorrect behavior or drift—shortcuts are still uniquely defined and consumed via getShortcut(). As stated, it’s not a verifiable defect or substantive review issue from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-shortcut validation in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit only detects size mismatch; a grant with "na" shortcut silently collides with the UNKNOWN sentinel mapping without detection

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, if a grant uses the shortcut "na" (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN), then the later sentinel insertion `grantsByShortcuts.put("na","na")` overwrites the existing value but does not change `grantsByShortcuts` size, while `grantsToShortcuts.put("na","na")` adds a new key ("na") in addition to the grant-id->shortcut entry, increasing `grantsToShortcuts` size. The subsequent check `if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size())` would therefore detect this as a mismatch and throw, so it is not a silent collision as claimed (based on what the diff shows).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted assertion in isAccessTokenId matcher in AssertEvents.java: returns false when the grant shortcut matches the expected grant and true when it does not, causing tests to fail on correct behavior and pass on wrong grant types

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, matchesSafely contains `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, which inverts the intended logic by failing when the grant shortcut matches the expected value. This would make tests fail on correct token IDs and potentially pass on incorrect ones. (Additionally, the substring indices look off for a 6-char context, but the inversion alone is a verifiable defect.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: substring(3, 5) in isAccessTokenId should be substring(4, 6) for a grant shortcut at offset 4

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the encoded token context format introduced elsewhere in the diff is 6 characters: 2 for sessionType + 2 for tokenType + 2 for grantType (see DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId and its comment). That means the grant shortcut occupies indices [4,6) of items[0], so using items[0].substring(3, 5) is an off-by-one error and will extract the wrong characters, causing the matcher to mis-validate token IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: items[0] shorter than 5 chars in isAccessTokenId throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of mismatching

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, after `item.split(":")` and checking only `items.length != 2`, the code calls `items[0].substring(3, 5)` without verifying `items[0].length() >= 5`. If the prefix part is shorter than 5 characters, this will throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of returning `false` (mismatch), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext constructor null check duplicated on grantType instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId to produce a token id like "onrtna:null"

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the last null-check mistakenly calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of validating `rawTokenId` (see `AccessTokenContext.java`). This leaves `rawTokenId` unchecked and allows constructing an `AccessTokenContext` with `rawTokenId == null`; `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` then concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would yield an encoded token id suffix of `"null"`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lazy map refresh paths in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut blindly put into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without re-checking for collisions, silently overwriting shortcuts on hot-deployed grants

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`, both lazy refresh paths can overwrite existing shortcut↔grant mappings without re-validating uniqueness. `getShortcutByGrantType()` does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` after loading a factory for a newly seen grant type, which will silently replace any prior mapping for the same `shortcut`. Similarly, `getGrantTypeByShortcut()` may `put(shortcut, newGrantType)` and update `grantsToShortcuts` based on the first matching factory found, again without checking whether that shortcut was already bound to a different grant. The only collision validation is in `postInit()` via size comparison, which does not cover these later refresh updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public Context(Context) copy constructor removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context, breaking existing third-party grant SPI implementations at runtime with NoSuchMethodError

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (see removal of the entire constructor block). Since this is a public constructor in a type used by grant implementations, any previously compiled extension/provider code that invokes `new OAuth2GrantType.Context(existingCtx)` would fail to link at runtime against the new binaries, producing a `NoSuchMethodError`. This is a real binary-compatibility break introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Remaining OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor NPEs if formParams is null, which the old copy constructor tolerated

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context` constructor, the diff adds `this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);` without a null-check. If `formParams` is passed as null, this will throw an NPE. Previously the constructor only assigned `this.formParams = formParams` and the removed copy constructor also merely copied the field, so null could be tolerated. The diff therefore introduces a concrete NPE risk in the constructor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId throws unhandled IllegalArgumentException on malformed token ids containing a ':' with a prefix not exactly 6 chars, instead of graceful UNKNOWN handling

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId`, if the token id contains `:` and the prefix length is not exactly 6, it explicitly does `throw new IllegalArgumentException("Incorrect token id...")` (and similarly throws for unknown shortcuts). The diff does not show any contract requiring graceful `UNKNOWN` handling for these malformed `:`-containing inputs, nor any call site demonstrating this is "unhandled" and causes broken behavior. This is a robustness/design concern rather than a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGrantTypeByShortcut/getShortcutByGrantType are non-atomic check-then-act: concurrent requests can race on lazy map population, leaving grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts temporarily inconsistent

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() lazily populate two separate ConcurrentHashMaps (grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts) with sequential put() calls and no synchronization. While each put is thread-safe, the pair of updates is not atomic across both maps, so concurrent calls can observe a partially-updated state (e.g., one map updated but not the other), potentially leading to transient null lookups and IllegalStateException/IllegalArgumentException in encodeTokenId()/getTokenContextFromTokenId().

adjudication_records.issue_text: PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process() sets GRANT_TYPE on a locally created DefaultClientSessionContext that doesn't flow through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, so the attribute may not reach initToken and the encoded id may silently carry "na" instead of "pc"

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process() now sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` on the `ClientSessionContext` it creates (`sessionContext.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_TYPE);`). The finding asserts that this locally created context "doesn't flow" to `TokenManager.initToken()` and thus the encoded token id would carry `na`, but the diff does not show the rest of `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process()` (i.e., whether `sessionContext` is or is not later used to mint the access token). Therefore the claim that the attribute will not reach token creation is not verifiable from the provided diff and appears to be an unsupported assumption.
